canonPolicy.rule: Fixtures demonstrate how different transit mathematics respond to identical geometry. They do not establish canonical speeds, ranges, constants, or historical events.

sharedScenario.description: A 12.0 ly origin-destination baseline with a massive stellar obstacle offset from the direct line, a broad low-gradient saddle, one unresolved companion-mass perturbation and a beacon-assisted alternate route.

candidateRoutes.character: shortest geometric line; strongest curvature and shear
longer normal-space path through broad low-gradient gravitational saddle
longest normal-space route; strongest reference quality and lowest fork ambiguity

familyCases.decision: Reject DIRECT despite shorter ordinary distance because curvature/tidal penalties consume field and recovery authority. P4 multi-sector solving makes the low-gradient saddle cheaper to deform coherently.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: distributed tensor sectors carry lower peak differential load but remain active longer; heat/recovery sizing follows integrated route burden rather than straight-line length
familyCases.abort: degraded abort remains available while sector closure and recovery reserve stay positive

familyCases.decision: Prefer the broad saddle because gravity is the roadway. The direct line crosses a ridge/fork region that is short geometrically but poor dynamically.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: gradiometer and plane-transition bandwidth dominate improvement; additional raw drive power cannot substitute for missing route observability
familyCases.abort: reroute to adjacent plane is preferred before full ejection while graph connectivity remains valid

familyCases.decision: Choose the beacon arc because Q-boundary correspondence and exit certainty outweigh normal-space path length.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: larger phase-reference stores and distributed adhesion control improve usable range by preserving exit windows, not by increasing normal-space acceleration
familyCases.abort: multiple predicted release windows remain available until shear correspondence falls below recovery threshold

familyCases.decision: Distance is secondary to the discrete address graph. Beacon assistance lowers alias and epoch uncertainty enough that a seven-hop route beats a shorter but weakly referenced address sequence.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: memory integrity, phase clocks, tomography and defect-correction capacity determine strategic usefulness
familyCases.abort: abort ends at indivisible address-transition commit; pre-commit anti-alias validation is therefore dominant

familyCases.decision: Select a six-axis geodesic whose normal-space projection follows the saddle because lower curvature improves embedding and return-map conditioning.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: additional axis resonators and topology sensors buy route freedom only if control and projection structures can maintain a well-conditioned return map
familyCases.abort: return-to-3+1D remains possible while at least one certified projection solution retains positive recovery margin

familyCases.decision: Route shape is mostly irrelevant after endpoint definition; beacon arc is selected because its reference network improves destination-state certainty and suppresses topology branch ambiguity.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: topology waveguides, aperture rings, recoil framing and endpoint metrology scale with protected volume and adjacency conditioning rather than cruise duration
familyCases.abort: once adjacency commit is crossed there is no meaningful steering; recovery-only logic applies

familyCases.decision: The dominant cost is infrastructure access, aperture scheduling and synchronization, not interstellar geometric distance.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: extreme topology machinery is concentrated in the gate complex; transiting ships primarily require compatibility, traffic control and safe approach systems
familyCases.abort: gate controller can hold, close or reject before throat entry; after entry recovery belongs to gate throat control

familyCases.decision: Ordinary separation does not dominate. The best destination is the most compatible, unoccupied, authenticated state target with acceptable continuity burden.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: tomography, immutable continuity records, biological/software state handling and quarantine capacity dominate system maturity
familyCases.abort: translation commit is discrete; unresolved identity/reference ambiguity blocks initiation rather than becoming an in-flight steering problem

model.trajectoryExpression: integrate relativistic acceleration/coast/deceleration subject to propellant and thermal constraints

familyCases.decision: No space manipulation occurs; shortest safe causal trajectory remains preferred unless gravity assists or hazards justify a detour.
familyCases.machineryConsequence: performance comes from exhaust velocity, mass ratio, power, thermal rejection and structural acceleration limits
familyCases.abort: ordinary propulsion shutdown/revectoring applies; there is no exotic no-abort topology boundary

generatorRules: All families must be evaluated against the same environment snapshot before comparison.
A family may optimize a different quantity than geometric distance; comparisons must expose that quantity explicitly.
A shorter ordinary route may be rejected because gravity, shear, phase, topology, reference, structure, coverage, recovery or infrastructure makes it more expensive or unsafe.
Tier improvements must identify the changed mathematical capability and physical enabler; unexplained scalar multipliers are invalid.
Runtime canonical speed/range data, when present, outranks fixture values.
Every numeric fixture must retain status PROPOSED unless separately adopted as canon.
